page: Microsoft Azure M96-48bds_2_v3 is a memory-optimized instance engineered for data-intensive enterprise workloads that demand substantial memory footprints and high-speed local disk performance. Built upon Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization, this virtual machine provisions 48 dedicated vCPUs derived from 24 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8473C processor running at up to 4.0 GHz. The processor architecture incorporates 105 MB of Level 3 cache along with instruction set enhancements including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). No dedicated GPUs are included in this hardware configuration.

Hardware allocation features 1946.0 GB of system RAM, yielding a massive memory density of 40.54 GB per vCPU. This configuration is paired with 4832 GB of high-speed local SSD storage, supporting high-throughput ephemeral staging and caching layers. In synthetic testing, the instance demonstrates high memory throughput, recording 301.98 GB/sec in large-block uncached memory read bandwidth and 156.64 GB/sec in large-block memory write bandwidth, placing it in the top quartile of evaluated systems.

CPU and I/O benchmarks highlight robust multi-threaded processing. The instance achieves a PassMark CPU score of 67,646.12 and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 319.69 GB/sec. In application-focused metrics, it sustained 66.02 million operations per second in Redis SET testing and strong marks in PassMark database execution. The presence of AMX instructions also supports CPU-based machine learning inference, generating 211.16 tokens per second during prompt processing on a 7B parameter model.

Because the server allocates an exceptionally high memory-to-vCPU ratio and includes substantial onboard SSD storage, it represents a specialized balance where infrastructure investment is targeted directly at large-scale memory residency. The primary tradeoff centers on the vCPU-to-RAM balance; workloads requiring raw compute scalability without memory utilization will find excess memory overhead. The M96-48bds_2_v3 is best suited for large in-memory databases, SAP HANA deployments, massive caching nodes, and complex transactional database clusters requiring substantial local scratch space.
description: Microsoft Azure M96-48bds_2_v3 is a memory-optimized virtual machine tailored for demanding in-memory workloads and high-throughput enterprise databases. Driven by Microsoft Hyper-V, the system provides 48 dedicated vCPUs from 24 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8473C processor clocked at 4.0 GHz, supporting AVX-512 and AMX instruction sets alongside 105 MB of L3 cache. It features an extensive 1946.0 GB memory capacity—averaging 40.54 GB per vCPU—and is bundled with 4832 GB of local SSD storage without integrated GPUs. Benchmark evaluations confirm upper-quartile memory bandwidth, achieving 301.98 GB/sec uncached large-block reads and 66.02 million operations per second on Redis SET workloads. The instance's resource density makes it especially cost-effective for large memory-resident architectures, though its high memory-to-CPU ratio makes it less appropriate for compute-bound tasks. It is best deployed for large in-memory databases, enterprise caching layers, and high-performance transactional systems.
